name: Letianpai Rux Robot
description: A screen-faced desktop AI companion from Letianpai (乐天派), a funded Beijing hardware startup — a round emoji-style face display, a 5MP monitoring camera, and genuinely functional bipedal legs driven by six servos, running a full Android-based OS with ChatGPT integration and an open developer SDK. It's sold under several different storefront names across marketplaces, including "QUJUSO" on some Amazon listings — same product, not a separate brand.

specs.label: Battery
specs.note: sources range from ~30 min to ~5 hrs — treat with caution

specs.label: Camera
specs.note: used for remote monitoring and video calls

specs.label: Movement
specs.note: genuinely walks on flat surfaces; has desk-edge fall detection

specs.label: OS
specs.note: open Python SDK; active firmware development on GitHub

specs.label: Subscription
specs.note: companion app is free with no listed in-app purchases

sourcing: Verified against Letianpai's own store and product microsite, its GitHub firmware organization (including direct inspection of its core repos' GPL-2.0 license files) and Facebook page, its Xiaomi Crowdfunding and Indiegogo campaign pages, a USPTO trademark record for QUJUSO, EqualOcean's funding coverage, a 36Kr/PitchHub investor profile, and independent reviews from Impulse Gamer, mia-cat.com, OriginOfBots, RoboticHunt, and a personal blog (Docandersen). Flagged as inconsistent or unconfirmed: screen size (2.1" vs. 2.4" across sources), battery life (30 minutes to 5 hours depending on source), current retail price (not independently confirmed from a live Amazon listing), the company's headquarters city (Beijing per its own site vs. Shenzhen per one press source), and a promotional claim that Letianpai's CEO is "the ninth founder of Xiaomi," which could not be verified. This entry corrects its prior name, which combined a reseller storefront name (QUJUSO) with the manufacturer's name as if they were a joint brand.

pricing.summary: Pricing is inconsistent across channels: a Xiaomi Crowdfunding campaign listed a full price of $469 (marked down from $599) before selling out, and a third-party robotics aggregator estimates an ongoing retail range of $299–469. This catalog could not pull a live, confirmed price directly from Amazon at research time, so treat any specific price as approximate until checked against the live listing.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: This catalog's original name for this entry conflated a generic reseller storefront, "QUJUSO," with the actual manufacturer; the robot's real maker is Beijing-based Letianpai, which sells the identical robot under its own name, with "Rux" as the robot's consistently-used real product name across every official channel. Letianpai's GitHub organization also publishes genuine GPL-2.0-licensed core firmware for the robot, confirmed against the repo's license file, earning this entry its Open Source badge.

firmwareCommunity.note: Letianpai's own official, GPLv2-licensed open-source system ROM for GeeUI, the software platform running on the Rux Robot.
